title: Password-Protect a PDF for Free, Right in Your Browser
description: Contracts, payslips and ID scans deserve a password before they hit your outbox. Here's how to encrypt a PDF in seconds with nothing installed.
excerpt: Emailing a sensitive PDF unprotected is like posting your house keys. Locking it takes ten seconds.
content:
You're emailing a contract, a payslip, or a scan of your passport. That attachment crosses a handful of servers, lands in someone else's inbox, and gets swept into backups. Unprotected, it's the digital equivalent of posting your house keys. Locking a PDF takes about ten seconds.

## When a password is actually worth it

Rule of thumb: if you'd mind someone printing the file and leaving it on a desk, it needs a password. That means contracts, invoices with bank details, medical records, payslips, ID scans. A brochure that already lives on your website doesn't — you're just annoying the recipient.

## How to do it with nothing installed

Open [FileTools.eu](https://filetools.eu), upload the PDF, set a password, download the encrypted copy. Processing happens locally in your browser, so the file never leaves your machine. Same flow on phone or desktop, no account, no Acrobat licence.

## Send the password down a different channel

This is where most people undo their own work: they attach the locked PDF and type the password in the same email. That cancels the encryption entirely. Send it by SMS, Signal, or say it on a call. And don't reuse one password across every document you send.

Ten seconds of effort, an order of magnitude less risk. Alongside encryption, [FileTools.eu](https://filetools.eu) also merges, compresses and unlocks PDFs — and if you record walkthroughs for your documents, [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) dubs them into other languages.
